**Supported fact**

Current official PDF.js docs present the **generic build as a browser-oriented prebuilt package**: the getting-started page says the prebuilt package “includes the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer,” and its examples page says its main tutorial shows use “in a web browser.” https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The same official examples page says there are separate `examples/node/` examples for Node.js usage. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The current official Node text-extraction example does **not** import the generic build; it imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

The public API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for a `TextContent` object, and that all whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`). https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html

The `TextContent` docs say it contains an `items` array plus `styles`; `TextItem.str` is the text string, and `TextItem` also carries direction, transform, width, height, font name, and `hasEOL`. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html

For Node-like environments, the current source explicitly warns: `Please use the legacy build in Node.js environments.` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

The current FAQ says PDF.js ships a default non-polyfilled build for the latest browsers and a separate `legacy` build for older environments; in its support table, `Node.js 22+` appears under the `legacy` build as “Mostly” supported with “Limited” automa

runs.final_answer:
**Supported fact**

Current official PDF.js docs present the **generic build as a browser-oriented prebuilt package**: the getting-started page says the prebuilt package “includes the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer,” and its examples page says its main tutorial shows use “in a web browser.” https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The same official examples page says there are separate `examples/node/` examples for Node.js usage. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The current official Node text-extraction example does **not** import the generic build; it imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

The public API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for a `TextContent` object, and that all whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`). https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html

The `TextContent` docs say it contains an `items` array plus `styles`; `TextItem.str` is the text string, and `TextItem` also carries direction, transform, width, height, font name, and `hasEOL`. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html

For Node-like environments, the current source explicitly warns: `Please use the legacy build in Node.js environments.` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

The current FAQ says PDF.js ships a default non-polyfilled build for the latest browsers and a separate `legacy` build for older environments; in its support table, `Node.js 22+` appears under the `legacy` build as “Mostly” supported with “Limited” automated testing. Bun is not listed in that table. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

The runtime defaults in `src/display/api.js` are environment-sensitive. In Node.js, `useWorkerFetch` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` defaults to `false`, `isImageDecoderSupported` defaults to `false`, `disableFontFace` defaults to `true`, and `useSystemFonts` defaults to `false` unless overridden. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

The same file defaults `ownerDocument` to `globalThis.document`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

In a generic build detected as Node.js, PDF.js switches its default factories to `NodeCanvasFactory`, `NodeFilterFactory`, and `NodeBinaryDataFactory`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

`node_utils.js` shows what those Node defaults assume at runtime: it uses `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(...)`, tries to load `@napi-rs/canvas`, polyfills `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` from that package when possible, synthesizes a minimal `navigator` if `navigator.language` is missing, and reads local files through `fs/promises.readFile`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

For worker setup, the API source says `GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc` “should always be set,” and `PDFWorker` creates a module worker with `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })`; in generic builds it also uses `window.location` for same-origin handling. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/worker_options.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

The current API source also uses modern globals/features such as `Promise.withResolvers()` and `structuredClone(...)`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

**Inference**

From those official sources, the **documented path outside the browser is “use the legacy build,” not “use the generic build.”** That inference follows from the Node example importing `legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, the explicit Node warning in `node_utils.js`, and the FAQ support table listing Node.js only under `legacy`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

For **text extraction only**, PDF.js appears less dependent on canvas rendering than for image rendering, because the official example extracts text with `getTextContent()` and only reads `item.str`; however, that is still an inference about practical portability, not an explicit Bun guarantee. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html

For **Bun compatibility**, the most relevant runtime assumptions documented by current official sources are: a Node-style `process` object, `process.getBuiltinModule`, `createRequire`, file-system access, optional `@napi-rs/canvas` integration, browser-ish globals such as `document`, `navigator`, `Worker`, and `window.location`, plus modern JS globals like `Promise.withResolvers` and `structuredClone`. If Bun diverges on any of those behaviors, the generic build could fail or fall back in ways the docs do not promise to support. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/worker_options.js

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

I found **no official PDF.js documentation in the sources above that explicitly says Bun is supported, unsupported, or tested**. The closest official support statement I found names `Node.js 22+` under the `legacy` build and does not mention Bun. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

I also found **no official source here that recommends the generic build for Bun specifically**. The available official material points to browser use for the generic build and to the legacy build for Node-style environments. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

**Disagreement**

I do not see a hard contradiction in the official sources, but there is a practical tension: the project distributes a generic prebuilt package, yet its current official Node guidance and runtime warning both steer non-browser usage toward the `legacy` build. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

## Scope and method

I checked the current `master` of `mozilla/pdf.js`, its published API docs, the FAQ wiki, and Bun's own compat docs. **No official PDF.js source mentions Bun at all** — a GitHub issue search for "bun" in `mozilla/pdf.js` returns only two issues where the word matched incidentally ([#20629](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/20629), [#19566](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/19566)), neither about the runtime ([search](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/search?q=bun&type=issues)). So everything about Bun below is **inference from documented Node.js assumptions**, and I mark it as such.

---

## 1. The generic build outside a browser — supported fact

**Building it.** The README documents two variants: `npx gulp generic` "bundle[s] all `src/` files into two production scripts and build[s] the generic viewer," emitting `pdf.js` and `pdf.worker.js` into `build/generic/build/`; `npx gulp generic-legacy` is the variant "if you need to support older browsers." Both scripts are needed, but only `pdf.js` must be included since `pdf.worker.js` is loaded by it ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md)).

**Official guidance for Node is the *legacy* build, not the plain generic one.** This is stated in code, not just prose. `src/display/node_utils.js` begins:

```js
if (isNodeJS) {
  if (typeof PDFJSDev === "undefined" || PDFJSDev.test("SKIP_BABEL")) {
    warn("Please use the `legacy` build in Node.js environments.");
  } else {
    // ...load @napi-rs/canvas, polyfill DOMMatrix / Path2D / navigator
  }
}
```

([src/display/node_utils.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js)). Note the consequence: in the non-legacy build the Node branch **only warns and does no polyfilling at all**. The official Node example matches this — it imports `from "pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs"` ([examples/node/getinfo.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs)), and the README points to that file and the `examples/node/` folder as the Node usage examples ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md)).

**Support level.** The FAQ lists Node.js 22+ under the *legacy* build's supported environments, describes support as "mostly" with "limited" automated testing, and summarizes: "Some missing features, but no problems in general" ([FAQ wiki](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions)). The repo's own `package.json` declares `"engines": { "node": ">=22.13.0 || >=24" }`, `"type": "module"`, and carries `@napi-rs/canvas` as a devDependency ([package.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/package.json)).

*Uncertainty:* that `engines` field governs the pdf.js **repository**; I could not load the `pdfjs-dist` npm page (HTTP 403) to confirm the published package's own `engines` or exact current version. The `pdfjs-dist` README itself is minimal — it only says it is "a pre-built version of the PDF.js source code… automatically generated by the build scripts," points to `legacy/` for environments lacking modern JS features, and defers to the main repo ([pdfjs-dist README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdfjs-dist/master/README.md)).

---

## 2. Extracting page text — supported fact

**API surface.** `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent(params) → Promise<TextContent>`, with the documented caveat: "All occurrences of whitespace will be replaced by standard spaces (0x20)." A streaming variant `streamTextContent(params) → ReadableStream` carries the same note ([PDFPageProxy API docs](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html)).

**Shapes**, verbatim from the JSDoc in `src/display/api.js`:

- `getTextContentParameters`: `includeMarkedContent` — "When true include marked content items in the items array of TextContent. The default is `false`"; `disableNormalization` — "When true the text is *not* normalized in the worker-thread. The default is `false`."
- `TextContent`: `items: Array<TextItem | TextMarkedContent>`, `styles: Object<string, TextStyle>` ("indexed by font name"), `lang: string | null` ("The document /Lang attribute").
- `TextItem`: `str` (text content), `dir` ("'ttb', 'ltr' or 'rtl'"), `transform` (transformation matrix), `width`/`height` ("in device space"), `fontName` ("Font name used by PDF.js for converted font"), `hasEOL` ("Indicating if the text content is followed by a line-break").
- `TextMarkedContent`: `type` ('beginMarkedContent' | 'beginMarkedContentProps' | 'endMarkedContent') and `id`.

([src/display/api.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js))

**The canonical non-browser pattern**, verbatim from the official example — note that `url` is passed a filesystem path, and that resources are explicitly released:

```js
import { getDocument } from "pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs";
const loadingTask = getDocument({ url: pdfPath });
// per page:
const { items } = await pdfPage.getTextContent();
console.log(items.map(item => item.str).join(" "));
```

with `pdfPage.cleanup()` after each page and `loadingTask.destroy()` at the end ([examples/node/getinfo.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs)).

Text extraction is the part of PDF.js least entangled with the DOM: it needs the worker/parsing path but not canvas. That last sentence is **inference**, though well-supported by the fact that the canvas factory is only reached via rendering, not `getTextContent`.

---

## 3. Runtime assumptions that affect Bun — the documented facts

Everything hinges on one predicate, `isNodeJS` in `src/shared/util.js`:

```js
const isNodeJS =
  (typeof PDFJSDev === "undefined" || PDFJSDev.test("GENERIC")) &&
  typeof process === "object" &&
  process + "" === "[object process]" &&
  !process.versions.nw &&
  !(process.versions.electron && process.type && process.type !== "browser");
```

([src/shared/util.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js)). It is a **duck-type on `process`'s string tag**, with no `process.versions.node` check and no acknowledgement of alternative runtimes.

That single flag then drives, in `src/display/api.js` ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js)):

| Assumption | Documented behavior |
|---|---|
| Workers | `if (isNodeJS) { this.#isWorkerDisabled = true; GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc ||= … }`, with the comment "Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there." Otherwise it does `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })` and falls back to `_setupFakeWorkerGlobal` (worker code loaded into the main thread via dynamic import) on failure. |
| Canvas / filters / data | `PDFJSDev.test("GENERIC") && isNodeJS ? NodeCanvasFactory : DOMCanvasFactory`, likewise `NodeFilterFactory` and `NodeBinaryDataFactory`. |
| Font handling | `disableFontFace` defaults to `isNodeJS`; `useSystemFonts` defaults to `!isNodeJS && !disableFontFace`. |
| Image APIs | `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` and `isImageDecoderSupported` both default to `!isNodeJS`. |

And in `node_utils.js` ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js)), the Node path assumes three more things:

1. **`process.getBuiltinModule` exists.** It is used three times: `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(import.meta.url)` in the polyfill block and again inside `NodeCanvasFactory._createCanvas`, and `process.getBuiltinModule("fs/promises")` inside `fetchData`. Only the first is wrapped in `try/catch` (`warn("Cannot access the \`require\` function: …")`); the two in `fetchData` and `_createCanvas` are unguarded.
2. **Data URLs are filesystem paths.** `fetchData(url)` is literally `fs.readFile(url)`, so in the Node branch `getDocument({ url })` reads from disk rather than over HTTP.
3. **Globals may be overwritten.** `globalThis.DOMMatrix` and `globalThis.Path2D` are assigned from `@napi-rs/canvas` if absent (with `warn("Cannot polyfill \`DOMMatrix\`, rendering may be broken.")` otherwise), and `if (!globalThis.navigator?.language) globalThis.navigator = { language: "en-US", platform: "", userAgent: "" }`. `@napi-rs/canvas` is `require`d optionally — missing it only warns.

---

## 4. What this implies for Bun — inference, not documentation

PDF.js's behavior under Bun is entirely determined by whether Bun satisfies `process + "" === "[object process]"`, and **I was not able to verify that from an authoritative source** — treat this as the open question:

- **If Bun passes the check** (`isNodeJS === true`): workers are force-disabled, so parsing runs on the main thread via the fake worker regardless of Bun's native `Worker` support; `getDocument({ url })` hits `fs.readFile`; and the `process.getBuiltinModule` calls in `fetchData`/`_createCanvas` must work or they throw uncaught. Bun's docs mark `node:process` as "mostly implemented" and list only `sourceMapsEnabled` and `addUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback` as missing — `getBuiltinModule` is neither confirmed nor listed as absent ([Bun Node API compat](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/nodejs-apis)). A third-party bug report claims `process.getBuiltinModule` is `undefined` under Bun alongside `DOMMatrix` errors ([pdf-parse#73](https://github.com/mehmet-kozan/pdf-parse/issues/73)) — that is **weak evidence** (downstream wrapper, unverified, possibly an older Bun), and it **conflicts** with Bun's own compat page. I'd want to confirm it with `bun -e 'console.log(typeof process.getBuiltinModule)'` before relying on either claim.
- **If Bun fails the check** (`isNodeJS === false`): PDF.js takes the browser path — `DOMCanvasFactory`, `DOMBinaryDataFactory` (fetch-based, so a bare filesystem path in `url` would not resolve), `disableFontFace` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported`/`isImageDecoderSupported` default to `true`, and a real `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })` is attempted. None of the `node_utils.js` polyfills would run.

Two further practical inferences that follow from documented facts: (a) since the official example and the in-code warning both point at `legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, that is the build to use under Bun as well — the modern build's Node branch does nothing but warn; and (b) for **text extraction specifically**, `@napi-rs/canvas`, `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` should not be needed, so the canvas warnings are likely benign for that use case — but PDF.js does not document this guarantee anywhere I found, so verify it against your own PDFs rather than assuming it.

**Bottom line on evidence quality:** parts 1 and 2 are directly documented and I'd rely on them. Part 3 is directly readable in current `master` source. Part 4 is reasoning from that source; no official PDF.js source makes any claim about Bun, and the one Bun-specific data point I found is third-party and contradicted by Bun's own docs.
